body_markdown:
If you have started using Claude Code, ChatGPT, or Cursor to help with sales work, you have probably hit the same wall: the AI is great at thinking, but it does not know anything about your actual pipeline, your sequences, or your buyers.


MCP servers are what change that. Here is what they are, why they matter for sales teams, and what the early use cases look like.


## What Is MCP?


MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It is an open standard that lets AI agents connect directly to external data sources and tools. Instead of copy-pasting context into a chat window, you give the AI a live connection to your data.


Think of it like an API, but designed specifically for AI agents to read and act on data from third-party tools. You connect an MCP server once, and then you can query it in plain language from inside your AI agent of choice.


## Why This Matters for Sales


The promise of AI in sales has always bumped into the same problem: the AI does not know your business. It does not know which accounts are showing intent this week, or who is on the buying committee at an account that just started evaluating a competitor.


MCP solves that. When your AI agent is connected to your sales intelligence data via an MCP server, you can ask:


• "Which accounts should my BDR prioritize this week?"


• "Which of our active sequences has the lowest reply rate?"


• "Which accounts started evaluating a competitor this week?"


• "Which of our customers are evaluating an alternative?"


And get a structured, specific answer. Not a general response, not a dashboard to navigate.


##
How GTM Engineers Are Setting This Up


The setup is simpler than it sounds. An MCP server exposes a set of tools that the AI agent can call. The AI agent makes a request, the MCP server queries the data source, and the result comes back in a format the AI can reason over.


For sales intelligence specifically, you are connecting your AI agent to the layer that holds your outbound performance data, your intent signals, and your contact intelligence. Once that connection is live, every question your team has about their pipeline becomes something an AI agent can answer.

##
Who This Is For


Right now, MCP is most useful for GTM engineers, RevOps leaders, and sales leaders who are already working with AI tools. You do not need to be a developer to use an MCP server, but you do need to be comfortable with tools like Claude Code or Cursor.


As AI agents become a standard part of sales workflows, expect this to become table stakes. The teams building these connections today are the ones who will have a structural advantage when AI agent workflows become the default way to manage a sales floor.
